questiontext.text:
The triangle \(ABC\) below has vertices \(A={@ntupleify(A)@}\), \(B={@ntupleify(B)@}\) and \(C={@ntupleify(C)@}\).

Using the construction tools provided, construct the escribed circle opposite \(B\) (the \(B\)-excircle).

GeoGebra displays the coordinates of the points you construct. Read off the position of the \(B\)-excentre \(J_B\) and the radius of the excircle (the exradius \(r_B\)), and enter them below, each rounded to 3 decimal places.

[[geogebra set="A__fixed,B__fixed,C__fixed" width="1200px" height="600px"]] params["material_id"]="vdqtbktj"; /* Restricted compass-and-straightedge toolbar. customToolBar OVERRIDES the file's toolbar; numbers are GeoGebra tool IDs, | starts a new menu. 0 Move, 6 Delete | 5 Intersect | 2 Line | 10 Circle(centre,point) | 9 Angle-bisector, 4 Perpendicular line | 38 Distance or Length. Provides 9 Angle-bisector and 4 Perpendicular line (perpendicular to the internal bisector gives the EXTERNAL bisector needed for an excentre), plus 38 to measure the radius. */ /* params["appName"]="geometry"; */ params["showToolBar"]=true; params["customToolBar"]="0 | 6 | 1 | 5 | 2 | 10 | 9 | 4 | 8 | 38"; params["showToolBarHelp"]=false; /* Hide the algebra input bar and menu bar. NOTE: the algebra VIEW panel is governed by the saved file (perspective is ignored with material_id), so ALSO close the Algebra View in the GeoGebra material and re-save. */ params["showAlgebraInput"]=true; params["algebraInputPosition"]="bottom"; params["showMenuBar"]=false; params["showResetIcon"]=true; params["showFullscreenButton"]=true; [[/geogebra]]
\(B\)-excentre \(J_B = (\,\) [[input:xc]] \(,\) [[input:yc]] \(\,)\) \( (\,\)[[validation:xc]], [[validation:yc]] \(\,)\)
[[feedback:prt1]]
Exradius \(r_B = \) [[input:r]] [[validation:r]]
[[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The centre of the escribed circle opposite \(B\) is the \(B\)-excentre: the point where the external bisectors of angles \(A\) and \(C\) meet (it also lies on the internal bisector of angle \(B\)). It is equidistant from line \(AC\) and from the extensions of the other two sides, so the excircle is tangent to side \(AC\) and to the extensions of \(BA\) and \(BC\). That common distance is the exradius \(r_B\).

Construction. Extend sides \(BC\) and \(BA\) and construct the external angle bisectors at \(B\) and \(C\). Their intersection \(J_B\) is the \(B\)-excentre. Dropping a perpendicular from \(J\) to extended side \(AC\) to the point of tangency) gives the exradius.

Provides 9 Angle-bisector and 4 Perpendicular line (perpendicular to the internal bisector gives the EXTERNAL bisector needed for an excentre), plus 38 to measure the radius. */ /* params["appName"]="geometry"; */ params["showToolBar"]=true; params["customToolBar"]="0 | 6 | 1 | 5 | 2 | 10 | 9 | 4 | 8 | 38"; params["showToolBarHelp"]=false; /* Hide the algebra input bar and menu bar. NOTE: the algebra VIEW panel is governed by the saved file (perspective is ignored with material_id), so ALSO close the Algebra View in the GeoGebra material and re-save. */ params["showAlgebraInput"]=true; params["algebraInputPosition"]="bottom"; params["showMenuBar"]=false; params["showResetIcon"]=true; params["showFullscreenButton"]=true; [[/geogebra]]

For this triangle the \(B\)-excentre is \(J_B \approx ({@dispdp(ta_EB[1],3)@},\ {@dispdp(ta_EB[2],3)@})\) and the exradius is \(r_B \approx {@dispdp(ta_RB,3)@}\).

node.description: Both B-excentre coordinates correct to 3 d.p.?

truefeedback.text: The centre is correctly placed at the \(B\)-excentre.

node.description: Did they find the incentre instead?

truefeedback.text: That point is the incentre — you used the internal bisectors at every vertex. For an excentre you need the external bisectors at two of the vertices. The \(B\)-excentre uses the external bisectors of \(A\) and \(C\) (each perpendicular to the internal bisector there).

node.description: Did they find the excentre opposite A instead?

truefeedback.text: That is the excentre opposite \(A\) — the centre of the excircle tangent to side \(BC\). You took external bisectors at the wrong pair of vertices. For the \(B\)-excircle (tangent to side \(AC\)) use the external bisectors at \(A\) and \(C\), with the internal bisector at \(B\).

node.description: Did they find the excentre opposite C instead?

truefeedback.text: That is the excentre opposite \(C\) — the centre of the excircle tangent to side \(AB\). You took external bisectors at the wrong pair of vertices. For the \(B\)-excircle (tangent to side \(AC\)) use the external bisectors at \(A\) and \(C\), with the internal bisector at \(B\).

node.description: Did they find the circumcentre instead?

truefeedback.text: That point is the circumcentre — where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet (equidistant from the three vertices). The \(B\)-excentre instead comes from the external angle bisectors at \(A\) and \(C\), and lies outside the triangle on the far side of \(AC\).

falsefeedback.text: Your point \(J\) is not the \(B\)-excentre. It is the meeting point of the external bisectors of angles \(A\) and \(C\) — check that each external bisector is perpendicular to the internal bisector at that vertex, and that it lies outside the triangle on the far side of \(AC\).

node.description: Did they give the inradius instead of the exradius?

truefeedback.text: That is the inradius — the radius of the inscribed circle inside the triangle. Here you want the exradius \(r_B\) of the escribed circle opposite \(B\), which is larger: it is the distance from the \(B\)-excentre to side \(AC\), equal to \(\dfrac{\text{area}}{s-b}\).

node.description: Did they give the circumradius instead of the exradius?

truefeedback.text: That is the circumradius — the radius of the circle through the three vertices. Here you want the exradius \(r_B\) of the escribed circle opposite \(B\): the distance from the \(B\)-excentre to side \(AC\), equal to \(\dfrac{\text{area}}{s-b}\).

falsefeedback.text: Your exradius is not correct (to 3 decimal places). The exradius \(r_B\) is the distance from the \(B\)-excentre to side \(AC\) (the perpendicular distance to the line it is tangent to), equal to \(\dfrac{\text{area}}{s-b}\).
